newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL LOSE UNBEATEN RECORD AT STRUGGLING RAYO VALLECANO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL LOSE UNBEATEN RECORD AT STRUGGLING RAYO VALLECANO.

text.p: Spanish league leaders Real Madrid lost their unbeaten record after playing their worst game of the season to go down 1-0 to unfancied neighbours Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday.
Real could see a lead which was eight points just five days ago reduced to only three if Barcelona win at Real Sociedad on Thursday.
The good news for Fabio Capello's side was that third-placed Betis could manage only a 1-1 draw at home to Celta Vigo.
Rayo, who fired manager Paquito Garcia earlier this week, scored through midfielder Ezequiel Castillo in the 35th minute.
They then survived several penalty scares to inflict the first defeat on Real in 25 league games.
"The refereeing was scandalous," Real chairman Lorenzo Sanz said. "For me there were three very clear penalties. Since the seventh game they haven't blown one for us."
Television replays suggested that Sanz may have been right.
Sanz also made vague threats afterwards to withdraw his team from the Spanish federation if a booking on defender Fernando Hierro from last Saturday's game with Betis is not overruled.

Hierro's absence through suspension together with that of fellow central defender Rafael Alkorta, who picked up his fifth yellow card in the game, could leave Real dangerously short at the back in their weekend fixture against Oviedo.
Real Madrid stayed six points ahead of Barcelona and nine ahead of Real Betis, who have a game in hand.
A nervous-looking Betis succumbed to a late equaliser after international striker Alfonso Perez had put them ahead at home to Celta Vigo.
A further three points behind Betis are Deportivo Coruna, who returned to their best form to come back from a goal down and beat Hercules 3-1
Champions Atletico Madrid, another point back in fifth place, scored a comfortable 2-0 victory over Logrones.
At the other end of the table new Zaragoza manager Luis Costa saw his side continue their recovery with a 5-0 win over Sporting Gijon, which looks set to leave coach Benito Floro in the firing line.
